Issue Detail Page | Issues | U.S. House Representative Yassamin Ansari Skip to content Close Home About Meet Yassamin Committees And Caucuses Our District Votes And Legislation Contact Email Me Newsletter Subscribe Office Locations Schedule A Meeting Website Problem Share Your Story Media Press Releases In the News Issues Services Flags Grant Applicants Help With A Federal Agency Internships Tours And Tickets Congressional Appropriations Request Congressional Art Competition Know Your Rights Service Academy Nominations FY27 Community Project Funding Requests Congressional App Challenge Community Ambassador Program Community Resources List Close Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari Modal Search Button MENU Facebook Logo Twitter Logo BlueSky Logo Youtube Logo Instagram Logo Home Issues Housing Rep. Ansari knows that housing is a human right, and she is fighting to lower the costs of rent and housing across the board. She believes that no one should ever have to choose between keeping a roof over their heads or putting food on the table, which is why she is a bold advocate for more affordable housing and transformative solutions to address the crisis of homelessness in Arizona and across the country. In places like Arizona, Rep. Ansari knows we don’t have nearly enough housing to keep up with our growing population. That means the cost of living is higher, rent is going up, and we’ve seen a spike in homelessness which is hurting families and our economy. On the Phoenix City Council, Rep. Ansari helped secure over $120 million in funding from the American Rescue Plan for rental assistance and new affordable housing developments. In Congress, she’s worked to advocate for additional funding for housing and homelessness mitigation programs from the Department of Housing and Urban Development.

Yassamin Ansari is the proud daughter of immigrants who came to the United States in pursuit of a better life. This country welcomed them, giving them the opportunity to achieve the American Dream. In Arizona’s 3rd Congressional District, over 64 languages are spoken—a testament to the rich diversity that strengthens our communities. Rep. Ansari believes that immigrants are essential to our culture, economy, and shared future. In Congress, Rep. Ansari’s first piece of legislation was a resolution celebrating the contributions of immigrants and opposing discriminatory immigration policies. She has also advocated for the American Dream and Promise Act and introduced legislation to recognize March as Iranian Heritage Month. She is committed to continuing to fight for the diverse communities of AZ-03. Rep. Ansari believes that we can have a secure border, be pro-immigration, and have an economy that works for everyone. In Congress, she will continue to push to secure our border and push for meaningful immigration reform that reflects the values of our nation and for a future where every Arizonan–regardless of their immigration status—has the opportunity to thrive.

Ansari understands that hardworking Arizona families are struggling to keep up with the costs of living, no matter how hard they work to achieve the American Dream. Too many in Arizona feel like they’re falling behind as wages fail to keep up with the skyrocketing costs of housing, health care, and everyday essentials. In Congress, Rep. Ansari is working for an economy that works for everyone—not just the wealthy. That means putting an end to the failed trickle-down policies and focusing on strengthening the middle-class and expanding economic opportunity. Since taking office, Rep. Ansari has introduced legislation to lower costs and make life more affordable for Arizonans—tackling everything from utility bills and housing to taxes and everyday expenses.

Ansari believes that the climate crisis is the defining issue of our generation. She came to Congress from climate advocacy, serving as the youngest climate policy advisor at the United Nations and helping to deliver the historic Paris Climate Accords. On the Phoenix City Council, she led the charge for clean air and water, created the first Office of Heat Response and Mitigation in the country, and helped pass the city’s landmark Climate Action Plan and Transportation Electrification Action Plan. Her work on the Phoenix City Council focused on reducing carbon emissions and improving the city’s air and water quality. In Congress, Rep. Ansari serves on the House Natural Resources Committee and as the Ranking Member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee where she is committed to working with her colleagues on legislation to combat climate change and build a more sustainable future. Since being sworn in, Rep. Ansari has cosponsored legislation disapproving of President Trump’s withdrawal from the Paris Climate Accords, supporting energy resiliency, protecting our federal lands, and advocating for clean energy jobs. She has also helped introduce the Heating and Cooling Relief Act with Senator Ed Markey to reduce home energy costs.

The Geothermal Gold Book Development Act establishes clear, consistent procedures and guidelines for geothermal leasing, exploration, permitting, and development. The bill directs the Department of the Interior, through the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), to create a “Gold Book” for geothermal energy, mirroring gold books already in use in oil, wind, and solar sectors. “I’ve spent my whole career working on climate policy; it’s humbling to see my first passed bill as a freshman make it through the House with bipartisan support,” said Ansari. “Harnessing the Earth’s internal heat through geothermal energy is a commonsense, promising source of renewable power. And my bill will ensure that the fastest-growing energy source in the United States can be safely regulated and reviewed by a nationwide, standardized system.” WATCH Ansari speak about her legislation. We are a nation of laws — not a nation of secret police, cold-blooded murders by federal agents on city streets, and blacksite detention centers,” said Rep. We need to pass my Drain ICE Act so that this horrific agency has not one more cent to terrorize American families and communities.” Ansari's remarks come after her eleventh congressional oversight visit. Last week, Ansari visited the Eloy Detention Center, where detained individuals reported lacking access to basic necessities.
